summary:
MALO_MARS_HiRes_Render (ARES-OS) is a full-stack planetary GIS, 3D mineral topography, and autonomous rover path-prediction platform inspired by NASA’s Perseverance and Curiosity localization maps. Designed as an interactive 2D/3D Mission Control workspace, it unifies real-time telemetry, orbital spectroscopy, granular laser altimetry, and cooperative robotics into a browser-based Mars navigation guide.

The multi-resolution canvas blends global CTX mosaics with on-demand MRO CTX (~6 m/px) and HiRISE (~25–50 cm/px) imagery streamed via NASA’s PDS ODE REST V2 API, alongside live GeoJSON rover waypoints from NASA JPL MMGIS for Perseverance, Ingenuity, and Curiosity. For astrobiology targeting, ARES-OS queries MRO CRISM and ESA OMEGA hyperspectral datasets, draping phyllosilicates, sulfates, and carbonates onto 3D elevation relief with adjustable vertical exaggeration.

Terrain safety leverages asynchronous MOLA PEDR laser altimetry jobs and USGS GeoTIFFs to generate topographic contours and flag >30° slopes as No-Go hazards. Adapting ETH Zürich ASL’s Informative Path Planning algorithm, the platform pairs a slope-constrained Rover Follower with an Aerial Scout to compute safe feasible and optimistic lower-bound paths until convergence. Finally, an integrated Mars24 chronometer tracks Coordinated Mars Time, Mission Sols, and Solar Longitude alongside an interactive atlas detailing all 11 historical Mars landers, rovers, and planetary landmarks.

MALO_MARS_HiRes_Render: Project Overview & Architecture

MALO_MARS_HiRes_Render is a high-resolution Mars planetary visualization platform, scientific GIS engine, and research cartography suite. It merges global NASA PDS data products with an interactive WebGL2 3D globe, progressive texture streaming, a high-precision 2D flat map, and the ARES-OS Mission Control science and autonomy layer.

1. What It Does & How It Works

- 3D Planetary Globe & Viewport Limiting: Powered by Three.js and WebGL2 on an IAU 2000 Mars reference sphere (R = 3,396.19 km). It implements a custom decontourification shader to smooth elevation steps and strict altitude clamping (minDistance = 1.08, ~270 km) to prevent texture pixelation.

- Progressive Texture Streaming & Level 5 GIS Pipeline: Streams multi-tier textures (2K -> 4K -> 8K master texture) alongside an underlying 134.2-megapixel global Level 5 mosaic (64 x 32 tile matrix derived from MGS MOLA + MEX HRSC Color Hillshade Blend at 200 m/px).

- ARES-OS Mission Control: Features a live Allison & McEwen (2000) Mars24 solar ephemeris engine, an IAU landmark atlas with namesake biographies, aqueous-mineral probability overlays, real USGS DTM slope-hazard analysis, and an Informative Path Planning (IPP) cooperative scout algorithm that proves route optimality and convergence.

- Authentic Rover Traverses & Landing Ellipses: Renders continuous single-line cartographic paths (THREE.Line) and scale-invariant precision point landing markers (THREE.Points) for Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, Spirit, Zhurong, and Sojourner, alongside NASA EDL dispersion ellipses.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

- Scientific Rigor & Accessibility: Bridges the gap between raw planetary data repositories (NASA PDS ODE, GDS MOLA) and interactive exploration, offering researchers and astronomy enthusiasts an intuitive way to inspect landing sites, slope hazards, and mineral distributions.

- Mission Planning & Autonomy Validation: Provides human EVA route planning backed by Minetti bioenergetics (0.38g metabolic cost model and 8-hour walkback envelopes) and cooperative scout path planning with strict optimality certificates.

- Zero-Dependency Lightweight Deployment: Runs efficiently out-of-the-box on a standard-library Python backend (server.py) with optional rasterio/numpy support for live USGS STAC COG DTM range requests.

3. Tech Stack & Tools Used

- Languages & Core Web Technologies: JavaScript (ES6+), Python 3.8+, HTML5, CSS3, GLSL shaders.

- Libraries & Frameworks: Three.js, OrbitControls, Leaflet (for 2D flat map reference).

- Backend & GIS Stack: Python standard-library multi-threaded HTTP server, optional numpy and rasterio for COG DTM range queries.

- Data Sources & Standards: NASA Mars Trek WMTS Level 5 tiles, GeoJSON, NASA PDS ODE REST API, USGS Astrogeology STAC.

4. Creativity & Design Factors Considered

- Visual Clarity vs. Clutter: Replaced bulky 3D tube geometries and oversized ground rings with razor-sharp single-line paths and scale-invariant point markers (sizeAttenuation: false), ensuring geological features and rover starting tracks remain completely unblocked.

- Seamless Dual-View Synchronization: Harmonizes the 3D WebGL2 globe and 2D hardware-accelerated canvas flat map so that camera positions, rover tracks, and selection states stay perfectly synchronized.

- Real-Time Ephemeris Integration: Dynamically calculates Martian seasons (Ls), Local Solar Time (LMST/LTST), and subsolar illumination angles, casting real-time shadows across the Martian topography.
